html:
A Czech playwright and dissident who led the Velvet Revolution of 1989 and became the last president of Czechoslovakia and the first of the Czech Republic. He lived from 1936 to 2011.

His family were rich, so the communist state barred him from university. He worked as a stagehand and became known for absurd plays such as The Garden Party (1963), mocking the empty language of bureaucracy. After Soviet tanks crushed the Prague Spring in 1968, his work was banned.

In 1977 he helped write Charter 77, a petition asking the regime to respect human rights. His essay The Power of the Powerless argued that ordinary people could resist simply by refusing to live within lies. He spent about five years in prison.

In November 1989, days after the Berlin Wall fell, mass protests in Prague brought down the communist government peacefully. Havel led the Civic Forum and was elected president that December. He served until 1992, when he would not preside over the split of the country, and was then president of the Czech Republic from 1993 to 2003. He led it into NATO.
